newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest dry this week, then wetter - Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest dry this week, then wetter - Smith Barney.

text.p: The U.S. Corn Belt should remain dry this week but long-range forecasts suggest a shift to a wetter pattern next week for the U.S. Midwest, said Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis in his daily update.

"This morning's (Monday) computer guidance indicates that by this weekend and next week (the week of August 11) there will be some changes in the pattern," Davis wrote. "Plain and simply, this pattern is much more favorable for widespread rains in the central U.S."
Davis said temperatures would remain cool this week with no widespread rainfall expected in Illinois until the weekend.
But Davis said a ridge of high pressure, which has kept parts of central Illinois unusually dry during July, will move west, changing the jet stream pattern and allowing for better chances of rain.
"The first frontal system which will move across the central U.S. and thus, be influenced by this new and improved moisture flow, will be from Saturday to Monday," Davis said.
"The bottom line is that all indications point to the Midwest and Delta going into a pattern which is more favorable for rains," he added.
